why_needed: The segment-1 pin applied the FIPS-197 C.1 known-answer vector at TEN ROUNDS ONLY and only for the real AES S-box (fips197_c1_kat_applicable is false for R1 and R2), and its 5120 encrypt/decrypt round-trips are invariant under any conjugation that enc_r and dec_r share. As recorded in segment 1, the random-S-box arms therefore had NO ABSOLUTE ANCHOR. The red team named this; it is now supplied.
what_was_done: an INDEPENDENT plain-Python FIPS-197 implementation (byte-wise SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns, no T-tables, no equivalent-inverse-cipher, no shared code or constants with the C probe) checked against the C probe's enc_r output for EVERY round count r=1..10, under the real AES S-box and under both random S-boxes. This is an absolute per-round anchor and is NOT invariant under a conjugation shared by enc_r and dec_r.
reference_implementation: ref_aes.py, plain Python, byte-wise SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns, no T-tables, no equivalent-inverse-cipher, no shared code or constants with src/yoyo_sbox.c

binary_tie_to_the_measuring_binary.purpose: tie the anchor binary yoyo_sbox_v2 to the MEASURING binary yoyo_sbox: identical arm output on short arms, so the per-round anchor validates the code path that produced the measurements
binary_tie_to_the_measuring_binary.v2_diff: src/yoyo_sbox_v2.diff (adds a read-only vec dump mode only)

what_it_still_does_not_cover: the anchor checks enc_r at every round count for all three S-boxes. dec_r is still covered only by the round-trip invariant against enc_r; since enc_r is now absolutely anchored, a shared conjugation is excluded, but a decryption-only error that the round-trip cannot see is not separately tested.
